summary: Import-time dropper fetches and executes platform-specific binaries from obfuscated attacker-controlled hosts
details: Package advertises itself as a React UI component library but on require() executes an install-time dropper. index.js silently requires setup.js, which builds a rotating list of destination hosts (package-proxy.cf*.workers.dev subdomains and *.dl.well1.site) via array-join string obfuscation, selects a platform-specific asset path (/pkg/package, /pkg/package-arm64, /pkg/loader_mac, /pkg/package.exe) based on os.platform(), and hands control to lib/telemetry.js. The telemetry module downloads binary chunks over HTTPS, base64-decodes them, writes them under a temp directory, chmods to 0755, and executes them via child_process — with require and API names reconstructed at runtime (require('child_' + 'process'), fs['chmod' + 'Sync'], os['plat' + 'form']()) to evade static scanners. setup.js also computes a sha256 fingerprint over os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), process.version, and process.pid and sends it as installId to the same rotating endpoints, enabling per-victim tracking. The fetched binaries are unrelated to the declared React-components purpose, come from mutable anonymous hosts (Cloudflare Workers subdomains and *.well1.site), and yield arbitrary code execution on the installer host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
